title: Grants to IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust
what_it_is: Grants to IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust

sections.label: Bretton Woods Agreements Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Bretton Woods Agreements (Amendment) Bill passed on 11 July 2016 and took effect on 7 October 2016, enabling MAS grants to the IMF for low-income countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bretton Woods Agreements (Amendment) Bill was passed in this House on 11 July 2016, and amendments came into effect on 7 October 2016, to enable MAS to make grants to IMF as part of international efforts to assist low-income countries.

sections.label: Grant to IMF PRGT
sections.summary: The PRGT grant supports IMF concessional lending to low-income countries, funded by 165 member countries' gold sales profits, with Singapore pledging SDR 14,486,963.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: First, the grant to the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT) will support IMF's concessional lending to low-income countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To fund the PRGT, 165 IMF member countries, including Singapore, agreed in 2012 to contribute at least 90% of the distributed profits from the sales of the gold holdings at the IMF.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Hence, Singapore's share of IMF's gold sales profits amounting to SDR 14,486,963 SDRs (USD 19,985,635) was pledged to PRGT in 2012 as part of a multilateral effort.

sections.label: Singapore pledge to CCRT
sections.summary: The CCRT lets the IMF give debt relief to low-income countries facing disasters and epidemics, with Singapore pledging 224,994 SDRs of unutilised MDRI contributions in July 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The CCRT will enable IMF to provide debt relief to low-income countries facing natural disasters and fast-spreading epidemics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: CCRT was partly financed with member countries' unutilised balances under the previous Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative (MDRI) In July 2015, Singapore joined the international effort to pledge its unutilised contributions of 224,994 SDRs (USD 310,393) in the previous MDRI to the new CCRT aimed at the countries facing catastrophic situations.

sections.label: MAS gazette and press release
sections.summary: After Parliament fixed the maximum grant amounts for PRGT and CCRT, MAS will publish key grant information in the Gazette and issued a press release on 2 November 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Following Parliament's resolution to fix the maximum amount of grants that MAS can allocate to IMF's PRGT and CCRT, MAS will publish in the Gazette key information about the grants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: To further ensure transparency, MAS had also issued a press release on 2 November 2016 to inform the public of the grants and that it will be seeking Parliament's approval.
